items.prompt: What is the main job of the heart in the body?

options.label: To make blood cells
options.feedback: Blood cells are made in the bone marrow, not in the heart. The heart pumps blood that already exists.

options.label: To pump blood around the body
options.feedback: That is correct. The heart is a muscular pump that pushes blood through the blood vessels to every part of the body.

options.label: To filter waste from the blood
options.feedback: Filtering waste from the blood is done by the kidneys. The heart only moves the blood, not clean it.

options.label: To store oxygen for the muscles
options.feedback: The heart does not store oxygen; it pumps blood, and the blood carries oxygen from the lungs to the muscles.

items.ok_line: The heart's main job is to pump blood around the body.
items.ko_line: The heart moves blood, not makes or cleans it.
items.exp_text: The heart is a muscular organ that contracts to push blood into arteries, which carry it throughout the body. Its pumping action keeps blood flowing so oxygen and nutrients reach all tissues.

items.prompt: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?

options.label: The left side
options.feedback: The left side of the heart pumps blood to the rest of the body, not to the lungs. The right side sends blood to the lungs.

options.label: The top side
options.feedback: The heart does not have a top side that pumps; it has four chambers, and both right and left sides have an upper chamber, but only the right ventricle sends blood to the lungs.

options.label: The right side
options.feedback: That is correct. The right side of the heart receives blood from the body and pumps it into the pulmonary arteries that lead to the lungs.

options.label: The bottom side
options.feedback: The bottom of the heart is just the lower chambers, and both left and right lower chambers exist, but only the right one sends blood to the lungs.

items.ok_line: The right side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs for oxygen.
items.ko_line: The left side goes to the body, not the lungs.
items.exp_text: The heart has two sides. The right side sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen, then the left side pumps that oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body.

items.prompt: What are the two upper chambers of the heart called?

options.label: Ventricles
options.feedback: Ventricles are the two lower chambers that do the main pumping. The upper chambers are the atria.

options.label: Valves
options.feedback: Valves are the flaps that keep blood flowing one way, not chambers. The upper chambers are the atria.

options.label: Septums
options.feedback: A septum is the dividing wall between the left and right sides of the heart, not a chamber. The upper chambers are the atria.

options.label: Atria
options.feedback: That is correct. The two atria are the chambers that receive blood coming into the heart from the veins.

items.ok_line: The heart's two top chambers are called atria.
items.ko_line: Atria are upper, ventricles are lower.
items.exp_text: The heart has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below. The atria collect blood that arrives from the veins and pass it to the ventricles, which then pump it out.
